method.gross: A gross is tickets: divide by the average US ticket price of its year for tickets sold, multiply by the 2025 price. Box Office Mojo's method.
method.budget: A budget is not tickets: scale by the US Consumer Price Index (CPI-U annual average) between the two years.
method.estimates: Ticket prices after 2019 are 2019's price carried forward by CPI, marked estimated, until a published figure replaces them.
method.runs: A film released more than once earned its money in different years at different ticket prices, so each release is restated separately: the original run at its year's price, each re-issue at its own, and anything the known runs don't account for at the original year's. The runs come from the old Box Office Mojo's Releases pages. For the 300 films on the old site's adjusted chart, its own estimate of tickets sold is used instead, because it splits runs the Releases pages lump together (Gone with the Wind's "1939" figure covers re-issues into the 1970s). A film with no known re-issues is restated from its release year alone.
method.runsShort: Each release restated at its own year's ticket price; what the runs don't account for stays with the original year.
method.example: E.T.: $359.2M in 1982 at $2.94 a ticket is 122.2M tickets; $40.6M in 1985 at $3.55 is 11.4M; $35.3M in 2002 at $5.81 is 6.1M. 139.7M tickets at 2025's $11.37 is $1588M, against $1683M if the whole $435.1M were treated as 1982 money.

sources.what: US CPI-U annual averages, 1982-84 = 100 (Bureau of Labor Statistics)
